limitations_and_boundaries: DDIMs are derived from a variational perspective and assume the same training objective as DDPMs; the non-Markovian forward processes are designed to match the marginals q(xt|x0).
The deterministic generative process (σ=0) is an implicit model, which may not capture full data distribution diversity as stochastic models.
Reconstruction error is evaluated only on CIFAR-10 test set; generalization to other datasets is not shown in these excerpts.
The speedup claims are based on wall-clock time comparisons on a specific GPU (Nvidia 2080 Ti) and may vary with hardware.
The interpolation and consistency properties rely on the deterministic nature of DDIM; stochastic variants (σ>0) may not exhibit these properties.

methods.name: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIMs)
methods.protocol_description: DDIMs are iterative implicit probabilistic models trained with the same objective as DDPMs. They generalize the forward diffusion process to non-Markovian processes, allowing deterministic generative processes that can be simulated in fewer steps. Sampling uses a non-Markovian reverse process defined by a parameter σ, with σ=0 yielding a deterministic implicit model. The model is trained using the DDPM objective Lγ with γ=1.

methods.name: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs)
methods.protocol_description: DDPMs are latent variable models with a fixed Markovian forward diffusion process that gradually adds Gaussian noise. The generative process approximates the reverse of this diffusion, requiring many sequential steps (e.g., T=1000) to produce high-quality samples.
